title: Wiki Documentation
shortDescription: A living documentation layer that turns any installation into a guided, repeatable process. Built in Notion and Figma, it gives every role, from technician to end client, exactly the instructions they need and nothing they don't.
longDescription:
It packages everything needed to install, operate, and hand over an interactive setup into one structured, living reference. Notion holds the searchable wiki, step-by-step procedures, troubleshooting databases, and role-based pages, all editable in real time, version tracked, and reachable on any device on the show floor. Figma carries the visual side: wiring and cabling schematics, projector mapping and calibration guides, floor plans, and branded handover one-pagers that make the whole thing client ready.

Its role flexes by audience. A technician follows the wiring diagrams and calibration steps, an on-site operator runs daily checklists and quick-fix flows, an event manager tracks status and sign-off, and the reseller or end client receives a clean, branded handover pack. The same source updates everywhere, so nobody works from a stale PDF. Tech partners keep standing access to the full wiki of tutorials and video walkthroughs, so the knowledge supports them long after the event.

It scales from a single kiosk to a multi-stand deployment, with QR codes on the hardware linking straight to the right page, optional multi-language versions for international crews, and content depth tuned to each role.

BRDGE builds and maintains the documentation layer end to end: information structure, version control, role-based access, and live links connecting every procedure to the module it supports.

highlights.title: Tech Partner Enablement
highlights.description: Tech partners get standing access to an extensive wiki packed with tutorials and step-by-step video walkthroughs. It turns setup, calibration, and troubleshooting into skills the team keeps, so partners stay self-sufficient across every future deployment instead of relying on a one-off briefing.

highlights.title: White-Label Handover
highlights.description: Drop in the reseller or client brand and the whole pack becomes a polished, professional handover. It makes a stand or installation feel fully owned and turns routine setup paperwork into a credibility builder you can charge for.

highlights.title: QR, Video & AI Add-Ons
highlights.description: Layer in QR codes on the hardware that deep-link to the right page, embed video walkthroughs, add an AI assistant trained on the docs for instant answers, or wire up live status dashboards and sign-off checklists. Each upgrade is an easy paid add-on.

highlights.title: Presentation Skins
highlights.description: The same content reskins to fit the moment: a lean technical style for crews, a premium branded style for client handover, a co-branded version for a sponsor, or localized regional packs for international teams.

highlights.title: Optional Usage Tracking
highlights.description: Add an optional usage-tracking layer to see what crews actually use: page views, checklist completion, install time, sign-offs, and recurring issues logged in a searchable database. In place, it cuts support calls, speeds every future setup, and gives clients clear evidence of a clean, on-time deployment.

highlights.title: One Hub for Every Module
highlights.description: It plugs into every other module by gathering each one's setup and run guide into a single hub. Pair it with Journey or Booths to document a full multi-stand route, with Games and Leaderboard to capture their config and reset flows, or with Visitor Identificator to brief reward handling, so a large deployment stays coordinated from one source.
